edit.description: `classify_directives` (src/graph.rs:1508) takes a backing *resolver* rather than the whole `repo_files: &[String]` slice: its only use of the set is `repo.contains(&resolved)` (src/graph.rs:1540), a membership test per cited `@import` target. Keep the predicate pure — the resolver is a parameter, two flavors (a fixed set for tests, the disk stat for the run), so the module stays testable with no disk dependency. The six in-module unit-test call sites reach it through the existing `backing()` helper (src/graph.rs:2700), so the helper's return type absorbs the change.

The disk flavor beside `repo_file_set` (src/compose.rs:1399): a stat membership test spelling the *same* predicate today's walk spells — `walkdir` with no `follow_links` collecting only `file_type().is_file()` entries under the harness root. Three verdicts must be spelled rather than inherited: a directory target is unbacked, a symlink target is unbacked (the walk sees a symlink file type, not a file), and a target resolving outside the harness root stays unbacked. This is a verdict-preserving fold, never a re-ruling of what counts as backed. `repo_file_set` and its `repo_file_set_count` pin stay — `reachable`'s `paths-match` channel is the remaining consumer.

The floor's unconditional `compose::repo_file_set(harness_root)` (src/gate.rs:383) moves behind the root `reachable` clause: the directive classing (src/gate.rs:396) takes the stat resolver, leaving `graph::reachable` (src/gate.rs:642) the walk's one consumer, and that judge already walks nothing where no root clause binds. The gate decides whether to walk (`engine::root_clause` over the assembled `selections`) rather than handing `reachable` a root path — the judge stays pure.

The `why` call site (src/read.rs:2484) takes the stat resolver. Its own `compose::repo_file_set(Path::new("."))` (src/read.rs:2479) stays: `graph::reachability_orphaned` (src/read.rs:2046) reads the whole set through `live_members`, and the read verb is not clause-gated.

The run-level count pin `a_full_check_run_walks_the_directive_backing_set_once` (tests/it/check_cost.rs:884) becomes the two-sided pin the cut earns: 0 walks over the bare-harness fixture it already builds (no root `reachable` clause binds), and exactly 1 over a harness whose lock carries one. Keep the non-vacuity assertion — the run must still have checked the fixture's members before either count is read.

The `repo()` fixture helper (tests/it/directive_classing.rs:41) returns the new backing flavor so its eight call sites stay as written; the absolute-harness-root case (tests/it/directive_classing.rs:214) re-spells against the stat flavor. New cases pin the three verdicts the stat test must reproduce: directory target, symlink target, outside-the-root target.

summary: Resolve an `@import`'s backing by stat per cited target; the whole-tree walk runs only where a root `reachable` clause binds.

per.section: Cost scale is hoisted, and pinned by count

tests.asserts: a full check run over a harness binding no root `reachable` clause walks the directive backing set 0 times, and exactly once where a root `reachable` clause binds
every backing verdict survives the stat resolver — a gitignored sibling is backed, a directory target and a symlink target are unbacked, and a target resolving outside the harness root is unbacked

acceptance: `cargo test` green with the two-sided walk pin and the three spelled stat verdicts; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
notes: Ruled by John 2026-09-29 (`(directive-backing-set-scope)`, via inbox): the backing set stays raw disk — `contract.md` "edge" says a path-resolved edge reads raw disk, never the discovery view, so folding onto the local discovery flavor would prune `.git/` and sub-corpus files and forge findings. The cut is resolution by stat, not a different set. scoped at e9573d2e
